findings.message: an indefinite article leaves which one open - use "the" and name the item
findings.detail: "The system shall write a log entry to a file" does not say which file, so two implementations both satisfy it and only one is wanted. The definite article names one thing, and a defined term is better still: the dictionary then says what the thing is. Sometimes correct: "a" quantifying a genuinely arbitrary member of a declared set ("any one of the four channels") — say the set, and the article stops mattering.

findings.message: 2 unbracketed and/or words - state the grouping, e.g. [X AND Y]
findings.detail: "A and B or C" has two readings and the sentence does not say which. Write the grouping down — "[X AND Y]", "NOT [X OR Y]" — so precedence is stated rather than inferred. Bracketing the expression clears this finding; so does splitting the sentence into one requirement per thought. Sometimes correct: two connectives joining plain noun phrases, not conditions, carry no precedence to get wrong.

findings.message: Sets a deadline but gives no time — add one (e.g. 50 ms)
findings.detail: This reads as a Sanad Timing requirement — the response names the obligation but the sentence carries no quantity with a time unit. A Sanad Timing requirement may resolve that slot from a value declared in the data dictionary instead of stating it inline, which is the better engineering of the two. Sometimes correct: the value may live in a linked verification requirement or an interface document this check does not read.
